reader.requirement: At --std 85 a RECORD DELIMITER clause in a sequential file control entry must be refused when the file's records are fixed length: a format 1 RECORD clause (VII.3.8.4 GR3) always, and no RECORD clause or a format 3 clause according to the implementor's documented record type (II.2.1.4.3, VII.3.8.4 GR13); a format 2 RECORD IS VARYING file (GR4) always admits it.

edition-consulted.switches: chooses the 1985 citation text in the COBOL7599 message; no behaviour

reader.edition-search: Read ScreenRecordDelimiter, HasVariableLengthRecords, RecordSizeVaries and ImpliesVariableFormat: none compares DialectLevel or Year; grep of FileControlBinder.cs RECORD DELIMITER arm shows only Edition.Cite/Edition.Error/Edition.Declined. DialectBehavior.RecordContainsRangeBindsRecordSize changes format 3 bounds enforcement at 85, not whether the records are variable length.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: one screen at every edition; only the cited clause numbers differ
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the 1985 witness covers format 1 with STANDARD-1; not no RECORD clause, two record sizes without a RECORD clause, an ODO record, format 3, format 2 accepted, or the implementor-names BINARY-SEQUENTIAL and LINE-SEQUENTIAL

probes.printed: EXIT 0, GOT [AAAAAAAAAA] for RECORD IS VARYING FROM 4 TO 10, RECORD CONTAINS 4 TO 10 (format 3), and LINE-SEQUENTIAL with no RECORD clause
probes.expected: accepted: variable length records (GR4; format 3 and the line sequential method variable by documented determinations DOC-A.1-148, DOC-A.1-150)

probes.printed: compiled; run: I-O status 44 on WRITE (the probe left the DEPENDING item SZ at zero)
probes.expected: accepted at compile time; a record size below the minimum makes the WRITE unsuccessful (VII.3.8.4 GR10)

probes.printed: COBOL7599 RECORD DELIMITER ... is specified for fixed-length records, for format 1, no RECORD clause with one or two fixed record sizes, an ODO record under format 1, and LINE-SEQUENTIAL under format 1
probes.expected: refused: SR1, the records being fixed length by GR3 or by the documented implied format 1 (DOC-A.1-147)

probes.printed: COBOL7599: no RECORD clause and no record description of it is variable-length ... fixed-length records (§1985:II.2.1.4.3; A.1 item 147)
probes.expected: implementor-defined at 85 (II.2.1.4.3); DOC-A.1-147 (b) documents an ODO record without a RECORD clause as implied format 1 counted at its maximum, so the refusal follows the documented determination

reader.notes: ScreenRecordDelimiter asks the one HasVariableLengthRecords predicate after the file description is bound and refuses with COBOL7599 for every fixed-length shape probed; the two implementor-defined cases of 1985 (no RECORD clause, format 3) follow DOC-A.1-147/148/150. The ODO-without-RECORD case is refused as fixed under DOC-A.1-147 (b), though 1985 II.2.1.4.2 describes such a record's length as affected by the DEPENDING phrase; the text leaves the record type to the implementor, so this is a documented choice, not a defect.

refuter.evidence: Probes at 85: src/r6-v1.cob (RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE, no FROM/TO, one 01 X(10)) accepted and reads back [AAAAAAAAAA]: format 2 is variable by GR4 even with one record size; src/r6-vto.cob (VARYING ... TO 12 only) accepted; src/r6-f3same.cob (RECORD CONTAINS 10 TO 10, format 3) accepted per DOC-A.1-148 (format 3 is variable here, GR13's latitude); src/r6-f1eq.cob (format 1 with two record sizes) refused COBOL7599 citing §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR3 and VII.2.8.3 SR1. FileModel.RecordSizeVaries keys on Varying (set for formats 2 and 3), so the record sizes do not override the clause's format. The no-RECORD-clause and ODO cases follow the documented DOC-A.1-147 (b) choice under II.2.1.4.3. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VII.2.8.3 SR1  (║2.8.3 Syntax Rules║)  the text is in SR1'; 'OK  §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR4  (3.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR4'; 'OK  §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR13  (3.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR13'; 'OK  §1985:II.2.1.4.3  (2.1.4.3 Implementor-Defined Record Types)  the text is in the clause'.
